text:
Matt Coronato opened the season as a power-play regular and a points player, and he has 17 in 25 games, eight with the man advantage. He's 24, a former 13th overall pick, and Calgary is trying to figure out where he fits best; one headline this month argued Ryan Huska should keep him with Matvei Gridin.

The case for patience is in where he shoots from. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts him at 8.5 scoring chances per 60 from the home plate in front of the net, 98th percentile among forwards. His finishing sits right on his expected goals (6 on 5.6), so nothing is running on luck. The weakness is at five on five, where the Flames take 46% of the expected goals with him on, about two points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, and he'll need more than power-play work to change that. Our range projects 46 to 67 points.
